ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Four vials were set up to investigate bacterial transformation. Vials 1 and 2 each contained E. coli bacteria that had been made competent and then mixed with a plasmid containing the gene for ampicillin (pAMP) resistance. Vials 3 and 4 both contained competent E. coli that were not mixed with a plasmid. Each vial of bacteria was poured onto a nutrient agar plate. Vials 1 and 3 were poured onto plates that contained the antibiotic ampicillin. Vials 2 and 4 were poured onto plates that did not contain ampicillin. The shaded plates represent extensive growth, and the dots represent individual bacterial colonies. Why were there fewer colonies on Plate 1 than on Plate 2?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: There was no antibiotic in the agar in Plate 2 that would have restricted growth of bacteria.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are four nutrient agar plates, labeled respectively as from test tubes 1, 2, 3, and 4. On plate 1 there are only a few scattered black dots, indicating a small number of individual colonies; plate 2 as a whole shows gray shading, indicating extensive growth; plate 3 has no obvious colonies or shading; plate 4 also shows gray shading, indicating extensive growth. Reasoning: The question stem explains that the initial treatments of test tube 1 and test tube 2 are the same, both containing competent E. coli and mixed with the pAMP plasmid carrying the ampicillin resistance gene. The key difference is that test tube 1 was poured onto a plate containing ampicillin, while test tube 2 was poured onto a plate without ampicillin. Ampicillin will inhibit the growth of bacteria that have not acquired the resistance plasmid, so on plate 1 only the small number of bacteria that were successfully transformed and acquired resistance can form colonies. Plate 2 has no antibiotic selection pressure and will not restrict the growth of untransformed bacteria, therefore more extensive growth appears.

method.method_draft: Identify from the image that Plate 1 has only scattered colonies while Plate 2 has extensive growth. From the text, note that vials 1 and 2 both contained competent E. coli mixed with the pAMP resistance plasmid, so their starting bacterial/plasmid treatment was the same. Then note the key treatment difference: vial 1 was plated on agar with ampicillin, while vial 2 was plated on agar without ampicillin. Apply antibiotic-selection logic: ampicillin on Plate 1 restricted growth to only bacteria that acquired resistance, producing fewer colonies, whereas Plate 2 lacked antibiotic and therefore did not restrict bacterial growth.
